tasks.short: Keep a periodic balance sheet of tender amounts and transaction numbers.

steps.what: Count notes, coins and card slips in the drawer.
Read expected totals by tender type on the point-of-sale till.
Copy expected and counted amounts onto a balance sheet.
Check transaction amounts that differ and note why.
Sign the period balance when the sheet is complete.
Mail the signed balance sheet and the till report.

tasks.design: The point-of-sale till {OTHER} places expected totals by tender type beside the count, and matched amounts form the balance sheet in {ERP}. The cashier writes a reason only when a line differs, and the store supervisor signs that sheet. Only the signed version is released; the cash-up workbook and the typed mail stop. The report is by till and shift, not by named cashier.
tasks.previous_blocker: Expected totals and the counted drawer were retyped onto a cash-up workbook and then mailed, so a difference waited for the next batch.
tasks.enabler_now: The till already computes expected totals per tender type at closing. Placing them beside the count is configuration, and releasing a signed sheet is an integration.
tasks.still_hard: Notes and coins are still counted by hand. A difference still needs someone who can say why, and a report that can name a cashier needs national works-council consent.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier knows which refund, pickup or mis-key explains a difference the totals cannot.

ambition.what: Review each tender-type difference on the day the till closes.

tasks.altitude: The cashier still counts the drawer each close. Retyping and mailing the sheet drop out. They do not gain the right to release a difference; the store supervisor still signs it.

reach.task: sign a till close that shows a tender difference
reach.learn: which fields (store, business date, tender type, expected amount, counted amount, variance note) are on the sheet before a signature

evidence.claim: Lightspeed X-Series closing shows expected totals per payment type and staff enter the count.
A till that already holds expected and counted tender totals can post a matched line and drop the mailed cash-up sheet. Model knowledge.
Under Dutch works-council rules, a tool fit to monitor staff, including a per-cashier variance report, needs consent, and so does a system that processes staff data.

assumptions: Workflow boundary is the cashier's close: from the drawer count to the signed sheet released to finance. Bank reconciliation and the ledger close are out of scope.

Structured fields are store id, business date, till id, shift, tender type, expected amount, transaction count, and counted amount. The cashier enters the counted amount. The till produces the expected amount and the transaction count. If the till has no closing export, the same fields are written on the closing slip.
Use the till's own closing screen before any custom code.
The store supervisor's signature is other-role time and is not sped up. Every sheet is signed, including a sheet with no difference.
Variance is stored by till and shift. A view by named cashier is out of scope until national works-council consent exists.
Three hours per 100 baseline hours keep the tender-type list and the variance threshold current. That upkeep is not zero.
unknowns: Whether the till already exports a closing total per tender type, or only a single grand total.
Who may set the variance threshold, and whether every close is signed today or only a close with a difference.
research_questions: What share of closes have a tender line over the variance threshold?
Does finance already receive the till close in the ledger, or only as a mailed sheet?

already_counted.description: The cashier still counts notes, coins and card slips. That time stays on the count step.
The cashier still reads each differing tender line and writes the reason.

incremental.description: Keep the tender-type list and the variance threshold current when a payment type is added or retired.

approvals.approved_version: signed balance sheet for this store, business date, till and shift, with tender totals and any variance notes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a close where the till already shows expected totals, retyping the sheet and mailing it drop out. The drawer count stays, and a differing line still needs a written reason. Stores that still copy from a paper till tape save less. Three hours of tender-list upkeep per 100 baseline hours are deducted. The supervisor's signature is not in the cashier's saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile and maintain non-monetary reports and records from the floor.

steps.what: Walk the floor and note gaps, damage and returns.
Pull item, void and return counts from the point-of-sale till.
Compile those notes into the non-monetary reports and records.

loop.input: floor notes plus item, void and return counts from the till
loop.output: record fields: item count, void count, return count, damage note, stock-gap note
loop.check: The cashier reads each label against the original note and rejects a label that changes the meaning.
loop.stop: One pass. A low-confidence line stays blank. No second model call.
loop.why_not_simpler: Floor notes are free text, not a till reason code, so a fixed column map cannot fill the damage and stock-gap lines.

steps.what: Recount a disputed item before the record is accepted.
Accept the weekly non-monetary record for the store.
File the accepted non-monetary record on the store file.

tasks.design: The point-of-sale till {OTHER} already holds item, void and return counts for the shift. A single pass proposes fields on the non-monetary record in {DOCS}, and the cashier rejects any label that changes the floor note. A colleague recounts a disputed count, the store lead accepts the weekly record, and filing replaces the loose page. Counts stay by till and shift, not by named cashier.
tasks.previous_blocker: Damage and stock-gap notes are free text from a floor walk, so they do not fall into a fixed column on their own.
tasks.enabler_now: The till already stores item, void and return counts. A bounded classify pass can propose the other fields, and a person still checks the meaning.
tasks.still_hard: The floor walk, the recount and the store lead's acceptance stay. A note with no clear meaning stays blank.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier saw the damaged item and the empty shelf. A count from the till cannot replace that.

ambition.what: Raise a stock-gap or damage note on the day it is seen.

tasks.altitude: The cashier still walks the floor and still checks the wording of the record. Pulling the till counts and filing the accepted page drop out. The store lead still accepts the weekly record.

reach.task: confirm a disputed item count on the weekly record
reach.learn: which fields (item count, void count, return count, damage note) must match the floor note before the recount

evidence.claim: A retail till already stores item, void and return counts, so those figures do not need a second transcription. Model knowledge.
Under Dutch works-council rules, a tool fit to monitor staff needs consent, and so does a system that processes staff data. A void list by named cashier would be that kind of tool.

assumptions: Workflow boundary is the cashier's non-monetary record: floor notes, till counts, a colleague's recount, the store lead's acceptance, and filing. Stock ordering and loss prevention investigations are out of scope.

Structured fields are store id, week, till id, shift, item count, void count, return count, damage note and stock-gap note. The till produces the three counts. The cashier's floor note is the source of the damage and stock-gap lines. If the note is blank, those lines stay blank.
The colleague's recount and the store lead's acceptance are other-role time and are not sped up.
Voids and returns are stored by till and shift. A view by named cashier is out of scope until national works-council consent exists.
Two and a half hours per 100 baseline hours refresh the reason labels. That upkeep is not zero.
unknowns: Which non-monetary records the store actually keeps (damage, voids, returns, stock gaps), and how often.
Whether floor notes are written at all today, or only remembered until the weekly page.
research_questions: What share of floor notes are a till reason code already, and what share are free text?
Who is expected to accept the weekly record, the store lead or the cashier?

already_counted.description: The cashier still walks the floor and writes the notes. That time stays on the walk.
The cashier still reads each proposed label against the original note.

incremental.description: Refresh the damage and stock-gap labels when the store's reason list changes.

approvals.approved_version: weekly non-monetary record for this store and week, with item counts, void counts, return counts and damage notes, as accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The floor walk stays. Pulling item, void and return counts, and filing the accepted page, drop out when the till already has those counts. Free-text notes still need a person to check the wording, so a store with messy notes saves less. Two and a half hours of label upkeep per 100 baseline hours are deducted. The recount and the store lead's acceptance are not in the cashier's saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise others and provide on-the-job training at the till.

steps.what: Supervise others during a live till sale.
Provide a demonstration of the next till step.
Write which training steps they can now do alone.
Decide whether they may work a till alone.
File the accepted training note on the store file.

tasks.design: A checklist in {DOCS} records which till skills were practised, while the live watch and the demonstration stay on the floor. The store lead still decides whether the colleague may work a till alone, and the accepted note is filed. No score and no emotion reading are added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Whether someone can work a till alone is a judgement made while watching them, and the store has no learning system for that judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: A checklist can hold which steps were practised. It does not need a model, and it does not decide readiness.
tasks.still_hard: Watching a live sale and showing the next step stay. A quiet hour and a busy hour teach different things.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier sees hesitation, a wrong tender key and how the colleague speaks to the customer. A ticked line does not.
tasks.altitude: The cashier still watches and still demonstrates. The blank page becomes a checklist, and filing the accepted note is no longer a separate copy. The store lead still decides who may work a till alone. The cashier gains no right to clear a colleague.

reach.task: decide that a new colleague may work a till alone
reach.learn: which practised skills are ticked on the note, and that a tick is not a score

evidence.claim: A checklist can record which till skills were practised. It does not judge whether someone is ready to work alone. Model knowledge.
Emotion recognition at work is a prohibited practice under the EU AI Act.
Staff performance monitoring is a high-risk use, and that classification applies from 2 December 2027.

assumptions: Workflow boundary is one coaching episode: watch a live sale, demonstrate the next step, write what was practised, the store lead decides, the note is filed. Hiring and formal certification are out of scope.

Structured fields are colleague id, date, till id, and a tick per practised skill (open the drawer, take cash, take a card, do a return, close the till). The cashier ticks them. The store lead produces the clearance. There is no score field.
The store does not run a learning system for this. The note lives in the store file.
The store lead's decision is other-role time and is not sped up. Any later change to the ticked skills voids the clearance and the filing.
One and a half hours per 100 baseline hours refresh the skill list when till steps change. That upkeep is not zero.
No model watches the colleague, and no emotion reading is used.
unknowns: Whether a written note of practised skills exists today, or the decision is only spoken.
Who may clear someone to work a till alone in this store.
research_questions: How many live sales does a new colleague work before they are left on a till alone?
Is the practice note kept, and for how long?

already_counted.description: The cashier still watches the live sale. That time stays on the watch.
The cashier still demonstrates the next till step.
The cashier still marks which skills were practised. The checklist only replaces the blank page.

incremental.description: Refresh the till-skill checklist when the till steps change.

approvals.approved_version: solo-till clearance for this colleague and date, against the skills ticked on the practice note
practice note for this colleague and date, with the skills ticked, as accepted by the store lead

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Watching and demonstrating stay in full. Only the blank-page note gets a little shorter, and only the filing of an accepted note drops out. A store that never wrote the note down saves almost nothing. One and a half hours of checklist upkeep per 100 baseline hours are deducted. The store lead's decision is not in the cashier's saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assist in other store areas, from fitting rooms to bagging items.

steps.what: Keep monitoring the fitting rooms while customers change.
Do the bagging of customers' items and carry them from the store.
Decide when a lift needs another person to help.
Read paid orders waiting for carry-out on the point-of-sale till.

tasks.design: The point-of-sale till {OTHER} can sort paid orders that are waiting to be carried out, so the cashier does not hunt through receipts. Watching the fitting rooms, bagging and carrying stay as they are. No camera is added in the fitting rooms or on the floor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paid carry-out orders sat in the same receipt pile as everything else, and the fitting-room watch cannot be done from a screen.
tasks.enabler_now: The till already knows which sales are paid and not yet handed over. A filter on that status is configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Customers changing clothes, heavy goods and the decision to call a second person stay physical.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier sees who needs a hand and when a fitting room needs a person nearby. A list cannot see that.
tasks.altitude: The cashier still watches the fitting rooms and still bags and carries. The only change is a shorter search for a paid order that is waiting. They gain no new right over customers or over the floor.

reach.task: see which counter orders are paid and waiting to be carried out
reach.learn: which handover status on the till means paid and not yet handed over

evidence.claim: A till that already marks a sale paid can filter the ones not yet handed over, so the cashier does not reread every receipt. Model knowledge.
Entering a shop is not consent to facial recognition, and a Dutch authority has warned a store that treated it as consent.
Behaviour cameras in shops have produced false alarms, and a necessity case is still required before they are used.

assumptions: Workflow boundary is floor assistance during a shift: fitting-room watch, bagging, carrying goods out, and finding a paid order that is waiting. Loss prevention and refunds are out of scope.

Structured fields for the list are order id, paid flag, handover status and a short item description. The till produces them from the sale. If a store does not mark handover, the cashier keeps reading receipts and this step does not shrink.
Fitting-room watching, bagging and carrying are unchanged. No camera, no facial recognition and no customer score is added.
Half an hour per 100 baseline hours adjusts the paid-order filter when a new handover status appears. That upkeep is not zero.
unknowns: Whether this store does paid carry-out at all, or only bags goods at the counter.
Whether the till already has a handover status, or only a paid flag.
research_questions: What share of shifts include a fitting-room watch, and what share include a carry-out?
How does the cashier find a waiting paid order today: a receipt pile, a shout, or a till list?

already_counted.description: The cashier still watches the fitting rooms. That time stays on the watch.
The cashier still bags items and carries them out.
The cashier still decides when a lift needs a second person.
The cashier still glances at the paid-order list before walking out with the goods.

incremental.description: Adjust the paid-order filter when a new handover status appears.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Fitting-room watching, bagging and carrying stay in full. Only the search for a paid order that is waiting shrinks, and only in a store that already marks handover on the till. A store with no carry-out saves nothing. Half an hour of filter upkeep per 100 baseline hours is deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week stays on the till and the floor. The mailed cash-up sheet goes away. The store supervisor still signs a tender difference, and the store lead still decides who may work a till alone.
reach: The store supervisor's tender-variance review can use the same till-and-shift totals the cashier already sees.
A department colleague confirming a non-monetary count can reuse the same item, void and return fields.
skills_to_grow: Read a variance line and write a short reason when the counted amount differs from the expected total.
Tick a till-skill checklist without skipping the live practice on the till.
Use the paid-order list without leaving the fitting room unwatched.
role.ambitious_version: Same-day close for every tender type, with a written reason only when the count differs, and a practice note filed before the new colleague's next shift.
